newsitem.title: USA: Calif. lab to pay $2.7 million settlement.
newsitem.headline: Calif. lab to pay $2.7 million settlement.

text.p: The University of California has agreed to pay the U.S. government more than $2.7 million for mismanagement of federal funds by Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory, officials said on Thursday.
The University of California manages the lab, one of two in the United States which maintain the nation's nuclear weapons, for the Department of Energy.

The university's governing regents have agreed to pay the $2.7 million to settle any potential action which the government could file against it for mismanaging the funds, the U.S. Attorney's office in San Francisco said.

"Public institutions such as Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory must maintain strict care and accountability of public funds since they have a public trust and responsibility to do so," U.S. Attorney Michael Yamaguchi said in a statement.
Its management contract allows Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory to do research projects for the Department of Energy and for other federal agencies.

The Department of Energy's Office of Inspector General asked for an audit of the J-Division of Lawrence Livermore's Applied Technology programme within the Nonproliferation Arms Control and International Security Directorate, the U.S. Attorney's office said.

The audit and investigation revealed that the lab, about 50 miles (80 kms) southeast of San Francisco, had mismanaged federal research and development funds between September 1990 and May 1993, it said.

The investigation found that more than $1 million in combined project costs for several project sponsors had been charged to other project sponsors and unauthorised loans had been made between unrelated project accounts, the U.S. Attorney's office said.
Lawrence Livermore said in a statement that no lab employee had personally gained from the transactions.

"To prevent recurrence at the lab, accounting practices have been reviewed and strengthened, training has been increased and additional audit and oversight have been established at Livermore," the lab said.
